angle: Value appears when AI owns steps end-to-end with guardrails, not just drafts.
sourceTitle: From assistance to execution: How enterprises put AI to work
linkedinPost:
Most enterprises are stuck in “assistant mode”—lots of drafts, few outcomes.

OpenAI’s piece on moving from assistance to execution mirrors what I’ve seen in the field: value scales when AI owns steps end‑to‑end with guardrails, not when it just suggests text.

Assistants shave minutes. Execution changes throughput. In customer operations, we’ve seen 20–40% faster resolution by letting AI gather context, propose an action, check policy, execute, and log—only escalating edge cases.

My take: don’t attempt a grand agent. Start with a narrow, frequent workflow (refunds under $50, password resets, product replacements in stock) and define: inputs, decision rules, allowed actions, and fail‑safes. Instrument everything—coverage, deflection rate, error rate, and dollars returned to the queue.

The litmus test: can you turn it off for a day and measure the capacity you lose? If not, you don’t have execution yet—you have a helper.

What’s the one repetitive process in your org that an agent could own safely by next quarter? #AIAdoption #CustomerExperience #EnterpriseAI #AIStrategy
